tools.access: Runs locally as a CLI over your repository and writes graph artifacts to disk; no account needed for local use.
tools.description: Turns a codebase — code, docs, SQL schemas, configs and PDFs — into a queryable knowledge graph an agent can traverse instead of grepping blind.
tools.name: graphify
tools.title: Graphify
tools.why: The shelf's founding entry: codebase comprehension as a tool, not a procedure — the one genuinely new capability from its reel checkup, finally given a home that is neither a skill nor the Void.

tools.access: Runs locally as a CLI (or via its web packer) and reads only the repository you point it at; the output is a local file.
tools.description: Packs an entire repository into a single AI-friendly file with token counting and ignore handling, for feeding a codebase to a model in one shot.
tools.name: repomix
tools.title: Repomix
tools.why: The complement to Graphify: when the job is handing a model the whole repository rather than querying it, this is the proven packer.

tools.access: Single local Rust binary that proxies common dev commands and compresses their output before it reaches the model; no account needed.
tools.description: CLI proxy that compresses common dev-command output (git, tests, builds) so agents spend far fewer tokens reading it.
tools.name: rtk
tools.title: RTK
tools.why: Token economy as a tool rather than a prompt trick: one binary between the agent and its shell, chosen over Headroom for the same job (simpler surface, no proxy layer).

tools.access: Desktop app that writes harness configuration files and stores provider API keys locally on your machine — review what it writes before enabling a profile.
tools.description: Cross-platform desktop assistant for switching providers, models and MCP configuration across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other harnesses from one place.
tools.name: cc-switch
tools.title: CC-Switch
tools.why: The harness-management job in one app: anyone running several coding harnesses otherwise hand-edits the same provider and MCP settings in each.

tools.access: Runs locally as a library or CLI and fetches only the pages you point it at; no account needed.
tools.description: Extracts the main content of any web page as clean Markdown, stripping navigation, ads and boilerplate.
tools.name: defuddle
tools.title: Defuddle
tools.why: The web-reading utility agents reach for first: page-to-Markdown extraction as a tool, not a procedure, from the Obsidian team.

tools.access: Installs session hooks and a background worker; captures session activity and sends it to a model for compression and recall — review what it captures before enabling.
tools.description: Persistent cross-session memory for coding agents: captures what the agent does, compresses it, and injects the relevant context into later sessions.
tools.name: claude-mem
tools.title: Claude-Mem
tools.why: The most adopted agent-memory tool in the wild; recorded with its capture-and-compress reach stated plainly so adopters decide with eyes open.
